q.t: In the fraction 3/5, what does the 5 tell you?
o: The whole is cut into 5 equal parts
q.e: The denominator (bottom) is the number of equal parts in the whole.

q.e: Double the friends, double the glasses: 5/4 = 10/8.

q.t: Which three DIFFERENT fractional units add up to 1?
q.e: In sixths: 3/6 + 2/6 + 1/6 = 6/6 = 1. It is the only way with three different units.

q.t: Why can't two DIFFERENT fractional units add to 1?
o: The biggest unit is 1/2, and 1/2 + 1/2 = 1; any smaller unit makes the sum less than 1
q.e: To be different, one 1/2 must be replaced by a smaller unit, so the total falls short. (2/3 is not a unit — its numerator isn't 1.)
